necessary_context.content: The norm is Euclidean. F(Delta,L) contains differentiable F:R^d->R with F(0)-inf_x F(x)<=Delta and ||grad F(x)-grad F(y)||<=L||x-y|| for all x,y.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.5, Notation and Section 2 Function class
necessary_context.name: Function class and norm

necessary_context.content: At round i, a measurable adaptive algorithm selects K points using its initial random seed and previous responses. A fresh independent z^(i) is shared by all K responses (F(x^(i,k)),g(x^(i,k),z^(i))). Function values are exact; E_z g(x,z)=grad F(x) and E_z||g(x,z)-grad F(x)||^2<=sigma^2 for every x.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.6, Section 2, equations (5)-(6) and Oracle classes; equation (2), PDF p.2
necessary_context.name: Optimization protocol

necessary_context.content: Additionally E_z||g(x,z)-g(y,z)||^2<=Lbar^2||x-y||^2 for all x,y, with the same sample z on both sides. This implies Lbar-smoothness of F.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.2 equation (4); p.6 Oracle classes
necessary_context.name: Mean-squared smooth Oracle

necessary_context.content: Equations (7)-(8) take sup over the relevant Oracle, sup over distributions on the function class, inf over A_rand(K), then inf over T in N such that E||grad F(x_A^(T,1))||<=epsilon. Expectation includes function, Oracle and algorithm randomness. T counts rounds; each full round returns K point evaluations sharing one sample.
necessary_context.name: Distributional complexity
